metaphors.text: turned my life into one long night seven times sealed
metaphors.interpretation: The experience is as oppressive and inescapable as a long night.

metaphors.text: transformed into smoke
metaphors.interpretation: The loss of identity is as complete as physical transformation into smoke.

metaphors.text: turned my dreams to ashes
metaphors.interpretation: The loss of hope is as complete as the transformation of dreams into ashes.

metaphors.text: The way is certainly both short and steep
metaphors.interpretation: The path to overcoming fear is challenging but achievable.

metaphors.text: The clothes that are considered right to wear / Will not be either sensible or cheap
metaphors.interpretation: True fulfillment cannot be achieved by blindly following societal expectations.

metaphors.text: A solitude ten thousand fathoms deep / Sustains the bed on which we lie, my dear
metaphors.interpretation: True growth and fulfillment require embracing solitude and overcoming the need for constant connection.

metaphors.text: hair sheened with gel
metaphors.interpretation: Joseph is presented as someone with a groomed and confident image

metaphors.text: the making of a small town myth
metaphors.interpretation: Joseph is presented as someone who will be remembered and talked about in hushed tones

metaphors.text: Word after sprawling hyphenated word
metaphors.interpretation: Time erodes language, just as it erodes youth.

metaphors.text: The glare of that much-mentionned brilliance, love, / Broke out, to show / Its bright incipience sailing above
metaphors.interpretation: Love is a light that can illuminate and solve problems.

metaphors.text: We know the rules and we are both pedantic
metaphors.interpretation: Formal social norms are being compared to the expectations of a romantic relationship

metaphors.text: Of the radio-phonograph
metaphors.interpretation: Love is like a radio program that broadcasts messages.

metaphors.text: Someone vomits; someone cries
metaphors.interpretation: Anxiety can be overwhelming and cause physical reactions.

metaphors.text: The Love that made her out of nothing
metaphors.interpretation: Love has the power to create and transform individuals.

metaphors.text: Chainsaw with its perfect disregard, its mood to tangle with cloth, or jewellery, or hair
metaphors.interpretation: The chainsaw represents the violent conflict between the man and the pampas grass.

metaphors.text: Corn in Egypt
metaphors.interpretation: The corn symbolizes the pampas grass overcoming and dominating the man.

metaphors.text: She folded them. I asked her was there a place where there was no world.
metaphors.interpretation: The speaker uses the action of folding hands to represent a state of peace and calmness.

metaphors.text: Her lips were the shape of a nipple.
metaphors.interpretation: The speaker compares the shape of the child's lips to a nipple to suggest a sense of helplessness and vulnerability.

metaphors.text: The fulcrum, at once she has power to lift me off the earth and keep me suspended by her tiny weight, she laughing, I stunned at the power of the formula.
metaphors.interpretation: The speaker uses the concept of a lever to represent the immense power of a child's potential for good.

metaphors.text: God in his wisdom made the fly
metaphors.interpretation: The fly is seen as a creation of a wise being

metaphors.text: What large, dark hands are those at the window
metaphors.interpretation: Love is like a powerful and grasping hand

metaphors.text: The bird lies warm against the wall
metaphors.interpretation: The woman is trapped in a relationship like a bird trapped in a nest

metaphors.text: His dark bright eyes descend like a fiery hood
metaphors.interpretation: The man is like a predator preying on the woman

metaphors.text: Taught me to hit, taught me to loosen
metaphors.interpretation: The emotional weight of the past is oppressive but can be overcome with the right approach.

metaphors.text: The space we stood around had been emptied / Into us to keep, it penetrated
metaphors.interpretation: The death of the protagonist's mother empties the family, but their grief and memories remain.

metaphors.text: The white chips jumped and jumped and skited high
metaphors.interpretation: The loss of the protagonist's mother leaves a void that is filled with a sense of emptiness and aimlessness.

real_concepts: Love as a threat to humanity

metaphors.text: Men adored thee and thy ways / All else above
metaphors.interpretation: Love is no longer as valued as it once was.

metaphors.text: We were but weak in judgment / We clamoured thee that thou would'st please / Inflict on us thine agonies
metaphors.interpretation: People now understand that they exaggerated their love and that it brings them suffering.

metaphors.text: No faery darts, no cherub air, / Nor swan, nor dove / Are thine; but features pitiless, / And iron daggers of distress
metaphors.interpretation: Love is no longer seen as gentle and beautiful as it once was, but as harsh and painful.

metaphors.text: busy archer his sharp arrows tries
metaphors.interpretation: Love is like an archer aiming and releasing arrows (desires) at a target (object of love).

metaphors.text: The nightingale with feathers new she sings
metaphors.interpretation: The changing of the nightingale's feathers symbolizes the passing of time and the renewal of nature in spring.

metaphors.text: The hart hath hung his old head on the pale
metaphors.interpretation: The hart's drooping head symbolizes the decay of summer and the passing of time.

metaphors.text: The busy bee her honey now she mings
metaphors.interpretation: The bee's gathering of honey symbolizes the joy and productivity of summer, but the mingling of honey also suggests a sense of sorrow or loss.

metaphors.text: Myths and fables of eld, Asia’s, Africa’s fables
metaphors.interpretation: Myths and fables represent spiritual stories and lessons

metaphors.text: Towers of fables immortal, fashion’d from mortal dreams
metaphors.interpretation: Fables are like towering structures built from human imagination

metaphors.text: You captains, voyagers, explorers, yours, You engineers, you architects, machinists, yours
metaphors.interpretation: Exploration and innovation represent human progress

metaphors.text: From the dull confines of the drooping west / To see the day spring from the pregnant east
metaphors.interpretation: London represents a place of new beginnings

metaphors.text: Give thou my sacred relics burial
metaphors.interpretation: London represents a place where the poet's legacy will be remembered

metaphors.text: Boot, saddle, to horse, and away!
metaphors.interpretation: The act of riding a horse represents the beginning of an exciting adventure.

metaphors.text: Snow-fairies falling from the sky
metaphors.interpretation: The conflict is like falling snow

metaphors.text: You danced and sang a lilting summer song
metaphors.interpretation: The passion is like a summer song
